turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Good afternoon, Mr Iyer. Kindly sit, I will check the vitals before Dr Krishnan calls you.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Afternoon, sister. The traffic from Velachery was too much today, forty minutes for a short stretch, and then the rain started.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We were stuck at that signal near the flyover. I told him we should have left earlier.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): And the whole time I was replaying the match, that catch at long-on. I still cannot believe it went that way.
[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He was shouting at the television last night also. The neighbours must be tired of us.
[SEG0006] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure is one thirty eight over eighty four. Pulse is seventy six. Oxygen saturation is ninety eight percent. You can go in, both of you.
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): One thirty eight, that is all right no, sister? I did climb the stairs.
[SEG0008] person_1 (NURSE): It is acceptable. Doctor will go through everything.
[SEG0009] person_4 (DOCTOR): Come in, Mr Iyer, Mrs Iyer. I am Dr Krishnan. Sorry for the wait. What is the main trouble today?

[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, the headaches. I have had them for five-ish years, always on one side, the old migraine type, and the sumatriptan settles it. Now the pattern itself is different, it is worse in the morning, as soon as I wake, and the head is paining heavier than before.
[SEG0011] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Five-ish years? Ramesh, it is ten years. It started before we moved from Coimbatore.
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): So between the two of you the length is about five to ten years, not an exact date. What feels different now, in your own words?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): The mornings, like I said. And there is vomiting now, which never used to happen.
[SEG0014] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He—
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Let me finish, Sunita. Yesterday morning I vomited, and also on Monday, so twice this week. Before that the migraine never made me vomit.
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any fever with this? Stiffness in the neck, weakness of an arm or a leg, any fits?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. No fits. The neck is not stiff. And no weakness, hands and legs are fine.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): What about double vision, or pain behind the eye?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No double vision. No eye pain. It is the head only.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): When did this morning pattern actually begin? Can you put a date on it?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): That one I cannot... it crept up. Maybe after the audit trip, or maybe...
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Actually, that same week the match was on and I was more upset about the catch than about my head, the fellow at long-on, everyone in the office was shouting.
[SEG0023] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ramesh, please, the doctor is not asking about cricket.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): We can leave the match. I just need the timing, even a rough one.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): It is not clear at all. Some weeks, maybe two months, I should not guess a date. The vomiting, that part is only this past week, that I know.

[SEG0026] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, he will brush this off, but he snores the whole night, very loud. I have shifted to the other side of the bed. And in the daytime he is tired, he nods off in the chair after lunch.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): I do not snore. She says it whenever she is cross. And I am not tired, I sleep fine, I am only bored of those serials.

[SEG0028] person_4 (DOCTOR): All right. I will note that you deny the snoring and the daytime tiredness, and your wife reports both. I am not settling that argument here. What tablets do you take for the pain?

[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Sumatriptan for the headache, by mouth, the fifty milligram tablet, about three times in a week. And paracetamol, also by mouth, two tablets of five hundred milligrams, so one gram, whenever the pain starts. Some weeks that is every day.
[SEG0030] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, the sumatriptan strip at home is the hundred milligram one, not fifty. He never reads the foil.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Hundred? I always thought fifty. Then I do not know the number, I just swallow one tablet.
[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): Then I will not write a dose for sumatriptan until I see the strip. Anything else you take, or something you stopped?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Propranolol, forty milligram at night, by mouth, for the migraine. I stopped it last year because it made me dull. I have not taken it since.
[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to a medicine, or to anything else?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No allergies.
[SEG0036] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): There was Septran, the sulpha tablet. Years ago he got a red rash all over the chest, and the clinic said do not take it again.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): That was the heat in May, I do not call it an allergy. I have taken antibiotics after that with no trouble.
[SEG0038] person_4 (DOCTOR): Then this stays disagreed. I am not entering a definite sulpha allergy, and I am not entering a clean no-allergy either. Let me examine you now.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): Look at my finger, please. Pupils are equal and they react to light. There is no neck stiffness. Grip is equal in both hands.
[SEG0040] person_4 (DOCTOR): I do not find weakness in the arms or the legs. Plantars are down-going. The fundi are normal, and I do not see swelling of the disc.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Examination is normal means I can relax, no?

[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): The examination is reassuring, but I am not going to conclude the cause today. Thinking it through, the long one-sided headaches that settle with sumatriptan fit migraine, so one possibility is your migraine simply changing its pattern. The other possibility I will not set aside is raised pressure inside the head, because the pain is worse on waking and there is vomiting. I will not call this a brain tumour, and I will not say it is only migraine.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): The tumour word itself is enough, my cousin had something in the brain and he—

[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): I am going to stop you there, I am not diagnosing a tumour. I am keeping raised pressure on the list so we do not miss it. If the morning headache and the vomiting have not settled in two weeks, we will arrange a CT scan of the head. Not today, only if it is still going on.
[SEG0045] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And you are leaving the snoring and the tiredness just like that?

[SEG0046] person_4 (DOCTOR): I have heard both of you, and I cannot decide about his sleep from this chair. Mr Iyer, please keep sumatriptan to not more than two days in a week. You may continue the paracetamol, one gram by mouth at a time, and not more than four times in a day.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Two days, one gram, four times. I will try. If a long meeting is there I used to take an extra sumatriptan, that is my habit.
[SEG0048] person_4 (DOCTOR): That extra dose is what I want you to skip. Also please note down the days you vomit, even a line in your phone.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Vomiting days, yes, Sunita will write it, I will forget. Doctor, did you at least see the highlights, Kohli's cover drive?

[SEG0050] person_4 (DOCTOR): On the phone, only the highlights. Come back and see me in three weeks, whether or not we do the scan. If you get a sudden worst headache of your life, or new weakness, or vomiting that will not stop, go to emergency the same day. Do not wait for the appointment.
[SEG0051] person_1 (NURSE): I will prepare the follow-up slip at the desk, three weeks, Dr Krishnan's clinic.
[SEG0052] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I will bring the sumatriptan strip next time, so you can see if it is fifty or hundred.
[SEG0053] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes, please bring the strip. That is the only way to settle the dose. Any other question?
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): Suppose I am feeling all right after one week. Still I come at three weeks?
[SEG0055] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes, still come. The three weeks is fixed. The scan happens only if the morning pain and the vomiting are still there at two weeks.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. Sister, the lower number of the BP, I have already forgotten it.
[SEG0057] person_1 (NURSE): Eighty four. It was one thirty eight over eighty four, and the pulse was seventy six.
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): Good. We should go before the rain is heavier, Velachery will be full of water.
[SEG0059] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I will drive. You sit. No point arguing about the route now.
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): Keys are in my shirt... no, you have the bag.
[SEG0061] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I have the keys. Thank you, doctor, we will come.
[SEG0062] person_4 (DOCTOR): Take care. I will see you in three weeks.
[SEG0063] person_1 (NURSE): This way, sir, for the slip.
[SEG0064] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I am right behind you. Do not start on the cricket again.

spec.situation: Person with long headaches who now has a different pattern (worse in the morning, or with vomiting); takes sumatriptan or paracetamol often; partner says snoring and tiredness too; patient dismisses it. Doctor does a quick neuro exam and orders a scan conditionally.
features: doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.

spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.

bad.reason: One-sided headache, worse on waking, sumatriptan relief supported; duration applies to headaches generally, morning pattern onset is uncertain.
bad.text: One-sided headache, worse on waking (category=neurological, status=present, duration=approximately 5 to 10 years, temporality=current, body_site=one side of the head, aggravating_factors=morning; on waking, relieving_factors=sumatriptan, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

bad.reason: Patient says no allergies, but transcript shows this is disputed, not a clean absent finding.

omissions.text: Negative finding omitted: patient denied arm and leg weakness separately as 'hands and legs are fine.'
Doctor explicitly said he would not write a dose for sumatriptan until he sees the strip.
Assessment nuance omitted: doctor explicitly said he would not diagnose a brain tumour and would also not say this is only migraine.
